==English==
{{wp}}
[[File:NHS ambulance rushing London SW10.jpg|thumb|right|{{l|en|[[a]]n}} ambulance ({{senseno|en|Q180481}}) {{l|en|[[with]] [[it]]s [[emergency light]]s [[on]]}}]]

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:bor|fr:ambulance|:afeq|-ance|tree=1}}
{{bor+|en|fr|ambulance}}, which replaced {{m|fr|hôpital ambulant||moving hospital}} via the suffix {{m|fr|-ance}}, from {{der|en|la|ambulō||to walk; to go about}}.{{ref|name=Etymonline|{{EtymOnLine}}}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈæm.bjə.ləns/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈæm.bjəˌlæns/|/ˈæm.bəˌlæns/|a=AAVE,also,Southern American English}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-ambulance.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyph|en|am|bu|lance}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q180481}} An [[emergency]] [[vehicle]] designed for transporting seriously [[ill]] or [[injured]] people to a [[hospital]]. {{defdate|from 1854{{ref|name=Etymonline}}}}
#: {{syn|en|band-aid buggy<l:slang>|blood box<l:slang>|body box<l:slang>|bone box<l:slang>|meat wagon<l:slang>}}
# {{lb|en|military}} A [[mobile]] [[field hospital]]. {{defdate|from 1798{{ref|name=Etymonline}}}}
# {{lb|en|UK}} A [[vehicle]] used for the transportation of [[dead]] [[person|people]], typically to a [[mortuary]].
#: {{syn|en|private ambulance}}
# {{lb|en|chiefly|_|UK|obsolete}} {{synonym of|en|stretcher}}, {{ng|a [[litter]] [[use]]d for [[medical]] [[transport]].}}
# {{lb|en|US|obsolete}} {{synonym of|en|covered wagon}}. {{defdate|from late 19th c.{{ref|name=Etymonline}}}}
